head: pr17457-r14
report:
## DEFECT: A held Cursor HTTP/2 run still writes tool results and heartbeats to Cursor after the hold engages

**Where:** `packages/ai/src/providers/cursor.ts`. `wrapHttp2RunTransport().write` (lines 819-821) calls `request.write(frame)` without asking the hold. Every write after the run opens goes through it:
- the exec/tool results, through `resultWriter` (lines 1591-1596);
- the KV blob replies (lines 2558 and 2579);
- the exec stream-close and throw frames (lines 3894, 3930 and 3948);
- the heartbeat sent every 5 s (line 1750).

The patch asks `admitSend` only when the session opens and the run request goes out (lines 1499 and 1510).

**Why it is unintended:**
- The other transports in the same patch gate every frame mid-stream: the Codex WebSocket `send` asks `admitSend()` per frame (`openai-codex-responses.ts:4320`) and so does GitLab Duo (`gitlab-duo-workflow.ts:2055`).
- Cursor's own HTTP/1 transport sends each append through `gatedFetch()` (`cursor.ts:881`, `:913`), so the same run over HTTP/1 stalls once held. Only HTTP/2, the default transport, keeps sending.
- The coding-agent changelog says a held subagent job "sends no further request at all … no model request (Anthropic's and Cursor's own transports included) … or WebSocket frame". The pi-ai changelog says "once the scope is held nothing it sends reaches a server".

**Impact:** coding-agent passes `cursorExecHandlers` (`sdk.ts:3960`, `:4735`), so Cursor's exec requests are answered inside the provider. Say a subagent's Cursor turn is streaming when its owner calls `beginDispose()`. Its local tool results still go to Cursor, and Cursor continues the agent step: more server-side inference, billed, while the job is supposed to be held. The file contents a tool read also go out.

**Reproduce:** `scratch/current__pr17457-r14__t2/cursor-h2-held-writes.test.ts`, run from `packages/ai`.
- Setup: a local h2c server answers `/agent.v1.AgentService/Run` with one `readArgs` exec frame. `streamCursor` runs inside `runInRequestHoldScope(held, ended)` with an `execHandlers.read` that blocks.
- Steps: once the handler starts, abort `held`, then release the handler.
- Measured: `{"bytesBeforeHold":185,"bytesAfterHold":71,"chunksAfterHold":2,"handlerResultReturned":true}`. The server logged "tool result text received after hold", meaning the read result's text arrived after the hold began.

**Fix:** gate `wrapHttp2RunTransport().write` on `admitSend()` the way GitLab Duo's `send` does: when refused, drop the frame and close the stream once the refusal rejects.

## NOT A DEFECT
Status of the earlier round's findings (reviewed at 12927ccd) at this head:

- **claude N1** (Anthropic `coworkFetch` on `node:https` sends after the hold): closed by reading the code. `sendCoworkRequest` now calls `admitSend(signal)` right before `https.request` with no await between (`cowork-fetch.ts:215-219`), and the fallback is `gatedFetch()`. I did not re-run the TLS probe.
- **claude N2** (`withAuth` resolves the credential, starting a refresh, before its hold check): closed by reading the code. `withAuth` checks `isRequestHeld()`/`admitProviderRequest` before the first resolution and before each later resolution and attempt. `withOAuthAccess`, `resolveRetryKey` and `holdAroundKeyResolution` do the same.
- **claude N3 / N7** (worker threads and child processes escape): now listed as escapes in the `request-hold.ts` header comment and in the coding-agent changelog. Intended, not a defect.
- **claude N5** (`AuthBrokerClient` captures `fetch` at construction): the changelog says it now reads the global per request. Not re-measured.
- **claude N6 / astra P1b** (restoring the global fetch ends the backstop): now documented as an escape, and the transports gate through `admitSend`/`gatedFetch` whatever the global is. Intended.
- **astra P1** (Cursor HTTP/2 sends the run after `beginDispose`): closed for opening the session and for the run request (`cursor.ts:1499` and `:1510`; the proxy tunnel at `proxy.ts:425`). It stays open for writes after the run opens; that is the defect above.
- **Not re-verified in this window:**
  - claude N4 (the checker misses `node:https`, a computed global and `new Function`);
  - claude F4d (`.es6` files);
  - astra P2 (shared reset redemption took the first caller's cancellation; the changelog claims it fixed);
  - astra's 14 checker attack shapes.

  I make no claim either way on these.

**Ruled out at this head:**
- `admitSend` and `admitProviderRequest` never resolve while held; they only reject when the scope or the signal ends. This matches the documented semantics.
- `holding` lets shared work through, because `currentRequestHoldScope` returns `undefined` for `SHARED_WORK`. That is the intended "its own fetches go out".
- In my probe the run request and the initial request-bytes write happen in the same turn as the `admitSend` check (`cursor.ts:1518`, `:1793`), so the opening race is closed.
